per_event.why: Both clips clearly show the ship moving, banking, and using the cyan scan/focus cone (e.g. X at 0:01, 0:03, 0:05; Y at 0:00, 0:01, 0:04). The visual and audio cues for movement and scanning are identical.
Neither clip shows single tap shots; the player only uses charged shots after resting or scanning.
Small scout enemies appear briefly and are scanned (e.g., X at 0:03, Y at 0:01 and 0:06), but none are shot, disarmed, or destroyed in either clip.
Both clips show the cannon charge meter in the top right filling up to 3 bars with identical rising audio cues and bright ship glow upon release (X at 0:00, 0:02, 0:04, 0:06; Y at 0:02, 0:04, 0:06).

Every charged shot in both clips hits the boss (X at 0:00, 0:02, 0:04, 0:06; Y at 0:03, 0:04, 0:06), producing a clear white flash on the heart boss and a distinct impact sound. Neither clip shows a miss for comparison.
No shots bounce off armor in either clip.
The boss takes damage to its health bar, but no parts or pods break off during either clip.
The player does not get hit or lose a life in either clip (hull stays at 3 bars).
Only single charged shots hit the boss one at a time in both clips; there are no moments with many simultaneous hits.

clutter.issue: Faint vertical dashed lines scrolling down the floor add minor visual noise compared to Y's clean floor, though bullets remain easy to see.
The warm reddish-orange floor color reduces contrast slightly with the pink/magenta enemy bullets and pink grazing rings compared to the darker grey floor in X.
When the ship charges and fires, the bright white/yellow bloom around the player ship is much larger than in X, momentarily obscuring nearby pink bullets right in front of the ship.

overall.why: Clip X has better contrast between the dark grey track floor and the pink enemy bullets, and the player ship's charge/fire glow is more contained than in Y (where the bright flash at 0:04 briefly obscures nearby bullets).
